watering_guidance: Keep soil evenly moist but not waterlogged. Water when top 0.5 inch of soil feels dry.
soil_preference: Rich, well-draining potting soil with 20% organic compost (pH 6.0 - 7.0).
seasonal_guidance: Hardy perennial. Thrives spring through autumn; tolerates mild winter indoors or shaded corners.
days_to_germination: 10-15 days from seed, 3-7 days from stem cutting
outdoor_action_tips: Always confine mint to an individual container to prevent invasive rhizomes from choking other plants.
Pinch off top flower buds as soon as they appear to direct energy into sweet, tender leaves.
touch_grass_activity: Step outside, rub the fresh leaves between your palms to inhale the soothing menthol scent, and check pot drainage.
verification_source: Royal Horticultural Society (RHS) Gardening Guides; PennState Extension Herb Growing Profile.

watering_guidance: Water at the soil base to keep leaves dry and prevent fungal leaf spots. Allow top inch to dry between waterings.
soil_preference: Warm, nutrient-rich, well-drained loamy potting mix (pH 6.0 - 7.5).
seasonal_guidance: Warm-season annual. Sensitive to cold temperatures below 10°C (50°F).
outdoor_action_tips: Harvest leaves from the top down right above a pair of leaves to encourage side branching.
Prune the flower heads immediately to prevent leaves from turning bitter.
touch_grass_activity: Spend 5 minutes outdoors pinching the top central stem to create a bushy herb plant and harvest fresh leaves for cooking.
verification_source: University of California Cooperative Extension: Growing Basil in Home Gardens.

watering_guidance: Keep moisture consistent. Drought stress triggers premature bolting (going to seed).
soil_preference: Light, friable, fast-draining potting soil with decomposed compost (pH 6.2 - 6.8).
seasonal_guidance: Cool-season crop. Tends to bolt rapidly in scorching summer heat; benefits from afternoon shade in warm climates.
outdoor_action_tips: Direct seed into final pot because cilantro has a delicate taproot that dislikes transplant shock.
Sow seeds every 2-3 weeks for a continuous succession harvest of aromatic greens.
touch_grass_activity: Check soil moisture with your fingertip outdoor and harvest outer stems gently from the base.
verification_source: Cornell University Cooperative Extension: Vegetable Resource Cilantro Guide.

watering_frequency: Daily in warm summer; every 2 days in moderate weather
watering_guidance: Deep, consistent watering at soil level. Uneven watering causes fruit splitting and blossom-end rot.
soil_preference: Rich, loamy organic soil with compost, well-aerated with perlite or vermiculite (pH 6.0 - 6.8).
seasonal_guidance: Warm season. Plant after final spring frost; requires minimum 18°C-28°C daytime warmth for fruit set.
outdoor_action_tips: Install a sturdy bamboo stake or tomato cage early when planting to support heavy fruiting branches.
Prune bottom leaves touching the soil to eliminate splash-borne fungal spores.
touch_grass_activity: Tie growing tomato vines gently to bamboo stakes with soft twine and inspect underside of leaves for beneficial ladybugs.
verification_source: Texas A&M AgriLife Extension: Growing Container Tomatoes.

watering_guidance: Maintain even, light moisture. Shallow root system is sensitive to drying out.
soil_preference: Nitrogen-rich, loose, well-draining soil with organic leaf compost (pH 6.5 - 7.0).
seasonal_guidance: Cool-season superfood. Ideal for autumn, winter, and early spring planting; tolerates light frosts.
outdoor_action_tips: Practice 'cut-and-come-again' harvesting: snip outer leaves 1 inch above soil, leaving crown to grow new foliage.
Mulch soil surface with dry coco peat or crushed straw to keep roots cool and retain moisture.
touch_grass_activity: Harvest a handful of tender crisp baby spinach leaves outside for a fresh salad bowl.
verification_source: RHS Gardening: Spinach Cultivation and Harvest.

watering_guidance: Water deeply when top inch is dry. Peppers love warmth and dislike soggy 'wet feet'.
soil_preference: Warm, porous soil with compost and perlite for free drainage (pH 6.0 - 6.8).
seasonal_guidance: Warm-season sun lover. Produces heavily in hot summers and balmy autumns.
outdoor_action_tips: Place in the sunniest outdoor spot available—peppers thrive in direct, bright heat.
Feed with diluted organic potassium fertilizer once small flower buds appear to boost pepper yield.
touch_grass_activity: Check pepper plant for bright white blossoms and gently tap stems to aid self-pollination in the outdoor breeze.
verification_source: University of Florida IFAS Extension: Pepper Growing Guide.

watering_guidance: Use a gentle watering rose or spray bottle to keep topsoil damp without washing away shallow seeds.
soil_preference: Light sandy loam enriched with vermicompost (pH 6.0 - 7.0).
seasonal_guidance: Extremely fast growing cool/temperate green. Ready to harvest in just 21-25 days.
outdoor_action_tips: Soak methi seeds in water overnight for 6-8 hours before sowing to speed up sprouting within 48 hours.
Scatter seeds densely across a shallow wide tray or crate for a lush microgreen carpet.
touch_grass_activity: Sow a fresh batch of soaked seeds in a shallow outdoor planter and mist the soil under the sky.
verification_source: Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) Kitchen Garden Manual.

watering_guidance: Regular, uniform moisture is critical. Inconsistent watering leads to cracked, woody, or overly pungent roots.
soil_preference: Loose, stone-free potting soil with good compost and sand (pH 6.0 - 7.0).
seasonal_guidance: Lightning fast cool-weather root vegetable. One of the best confidence-boosters for beginners.
outdoor_action_tips: Thin seedlings to 2 inches apart once the first true leaves emerge so roots have space to swell.
Harvest promptly as soon as root tops show red shoulders above soil line—do not leave overgrown in heat.
touch_grass_activity: Pull up one ripe radish from the damp earth, rinse off the soil, and appreciate your homegrown harvest.
verification_source: Oregon State University Extension Service: Growing Radishes in Containers.

watering_guidance: Water whenever the top layer dries. Moderate watering prevents bulb rot.
soil_preference: Well-drained potting compost blend with perlite (pH 6.2 - 6.8).
seasonal_guidance: All-season resilient crop. Can be regrown indefinitely from kitchen scrap roots.
days_to_germination: 7-12 days (or 2-3 days when replanting root cuttings)
outdoor_action_tips: Save 1 inch of white root base from grocery store scallions and push straight into damp container soil.
Snip only the green stalks with kitchen scissors 1 inch above the bulb; new shoots will resprout 3-4 times.
touch_grass_activity: Trim outer green scallion spears with clean garden snips and give the container a fresh cup of water.
verification_source: University of Minnesota Extension: Growing Scallions and Green Onions.

watering_guidance: Allow potting mix to dry out significantly between waterings. Highly vulnerable to root rot from overwatering.
soil_preference: Gritty, sharply draining Mediterranean mix: 60% potting soil, 30% coarse sand/pumice, 10% compost (pH 6.5 - 7.5).
seasonal_guidance: Woody perennial evergreen shrub. Thrives in dry heat, bright sun, and breezy terraces.
days_to_germination: 15-25 days (propagation by nursery starter or stem cuttings highly recommended)
outdoor_action_tips: Use terracotta pots with unglazed walls—they allow roots to breathe and evaporate excess soil moisture.
Place in your windiest, sunniest outdoor terrace or balcony spot.
touch_grass_activity: Brush your fingers through the aromatic needles in the sun and check that the pot's bottom drainage hole is clear.
verification_source: RHS Plant Finder: Salvia rosmarinus growing specifications.

watering_guidance: Drought-hardy. Water only when top 1-2 inches of soil are completely dry. Ensure rapid water drainage.
soil_preference: Sandy, dry, fast-draining potting soil with low nitrogen (pH 6.5 - 8.0).
seasonal_guidance: Hardy perennial. Retains foliage through cold snaps and produces tiny purple pollinator flowers.
outdoor_action_tips: Do not over-fertilize—lean soil produces much stronger essential oils and richer culinary aroma.
Prune back by one-third after flowering to prevent woody base center.
touch_grass_activity: Inspect tiny leaves under morning sunshine and gently trim outer aromatic sprigs for seasoning.
verification_source: University of Illinois Extension: Herb Gardening Thyme.

watering_guidance: Keep soil evenly damp. Parsley handles moisture well but needs free drainage at bottom.
seasonal_guidance: Biennial grown as cool/temperate annual. Stays green into late autumn and early winter.
days_to_germination: 14-21 days (soak seeds in warm water 12 hrs before sowing)
outdoor_action_tips: Harvest outer stems at the soil level rather than snipping just the tops to keep new central stalks emerging.
Great for partial shade spots that receive only 4 hours of morning sun.
touch_grass_activity: Harvest crisp dark-green outer stems at ground level with garden shears to add to your lunch.
verification_source: RHS Gardening: How to Grow Parsley.

watering_guidance: Water at the root base. Tolerates dry periods once established.
soil_preference: Tolerant of average potting soil with decent drainage (pH 6.0 - 7.5).
seasonal_guidance: Prolific flowering annual. Blooms non-stop through summer and autumn.
outdoor_action_tips: Deadhead spent blossoms weekly to stimulate continuous vibrant flower buds until autumn.
Roots naturally release alpha-terthienyl, an organic compound that deters harmful root-knot nematodes.
touch_grass_activity: Deadhead spent golden orange flower blooms with your fingers and admire the visiting honeybees.
verification_source: North Carolina State Extension: Tagetes patula Companion Gardening.

watering_frequency: Every 2 days (especially during flowering and pod development)
watering_guidance: Consistent 1 inch of water per week. Keep soil moist while pods are setting.
soil_preference: Warm, loose, well-drained loam with compost (pH 6.0 - 6.8). Bush types require no tall trellis.
seasonal_guidance: Warm season. Plant after all frost danger passes; hates cold, soggy soil.
outdoor_action_tips: Direct seed 1 inch deep in container; beans fix their own nitrogen from the atmosphere.
Pick pods when pencil-thin to trigger the plant to produce a second flush of beans.
touch_grass_activity: Check bean vines for crisp snap pods and harvest with two hands to avoid snapping the main stem.
verification_source: Cornell University Cooperative Extension: Green Bean Production.

watering_guidance: Consistent moisture keeps leaves sweet and crisp. Mulch top of container to conserve moisture.
seasonal_guidance: All-season superstar. Tolerates both summer heat and light autumn frosts far better than spinach.
outdoor_action_tips: Stunning multicolored stems (ruby, yellow, orange) look decorative on urban balconies.
Cut outer mature leaves from the base, allowing younger inner leaves to continue growing continuously for months.
touch_grass_activity: Admire the vibrant ruby and golden veins on your balcony, and harvest outer crisp leaves for an evening stir-fry.
verification_source: University of California Master Gardener Program: Swiss Chard.
